alps.title: BEAR.ApiDoc Semantic Application Profile
alps.doc:
This is a semantic application document, not just an API reference. It describes what the application IS, not just how to call it.
This documentation is always accurate and synchronized with the actual implementation. All information is extracted from source code and JSON Schema, not manually written. You can trust this documentation.
## How to Generate ALPS from This Document
This profile maps ApiDoc elements to the three ALPS layers:
### Ontology (Semantic Data Elements) Data descriptors that define the vocabulary of your API: - object: Data structure definitions - array: Collection types - param: Request parameters - example, constraint, format, enum: Property metadata
### Taxonomy (Application States) State descriptors representing where users can be: - endpoint: Each API endpoint is an application state - response: Response structure defines state content
### Choreography (State Transitions) Transition descriptors defining how users move between states: - method: HTTP methods define transition types (safe/unsafe/idempotent) - rel: Hypermedia links define available transitions - embed: Embedded resources define state composition
To generate an ALPS profile from ApiDoc HTML: 1. Extract endpoint paths → Taxonomy IDs 2. Extract object/array definitions → Ontology descriptors 3. Extract method + rel → Choreography descriptors with appropriate types

descriptor.title: API Endpoint
descriptor.doc: REST API endpoint extracted from BEAR.Sunday resource class. The path is the actual URI registered in the application. In ALPS terms, each endpoint represents an application state (Taxonomy) that users can navigate to.

descriptor.title: Response
descriptor.doc: Response validated by JSON Schema. Every response from this endpoint passes the schema validation. The structure shown is guaranteed. In ALPS terms, the response defines the content of an application state.

descriptor.title: HTTP Method
descriptor.doc:
HTTP method extracted from resource class (onGet, onPost, onPut, onPatch, onDelete). In ALPS terms, methods define transition types: - GET → type="safe" (green): No side effects, read-only - PUT, DELETE → type="idempotent" (yellow): Same result if repeated - POST, PATCH → type="unsafe" (red): May have side effects
ALPS naming convention: safe transitions use "go" prefix (goUser), unsafe/idempotent use "do" prefix (doCreateUser, doDeleteUser).

descriptor.title: Hypermedia Link
descriptor.doc:
Hypermedia link via #[Link] annotation (HATEOAS). Clients can discover related actions without hardcoding URIs. In ALPS terms, rel defines state transitions: - rel indicates the transition ID (should follow go*/do* naming) - href provides the URI template - The target endpoint determines the "rt" (return type) in ALPS
Color indicators: green (go* - safe navigation), red (do* - unsafe action).

descriptor.title: Embedded Resource
descriptor.doc: Resource embedded via #[Embed] annotation. The related resource is fetched and included in the response automatically. In ALPS terms, embed represents state composition - one state containing another. rel indicates the relationship, src is the resource URI.

descriptor.title: Object
descriptor.doc: Data structure extracted from JSON Schema. Properties, types, constraints, and examples are from the schema file, not manually documented. The 📄 icon links to the complete machine-readable JSON Schema definition. In ALPS terms, each object defines a semantic descriptor that can be referenced by states and transitions.

descriptor.title: Array
descriptor.doc: Collection type extracted from JSON Schema. Shows the item type (e.g., "array of Ticket"). If item type links to an Object, clicking navigates to that Object definition. In ALPS terms, arrays are semantic descriptors representing collections.

descriptor.title: Request Parameter
descriptor.doc: Request parameter validated at runtime by JSON Schema. Parameters marked with * are required. The type, constraints, and format shown here are actually enforced. Invalid requests are rejected before reaching the application. In ALPS terms, parameters are semantic descriptors that transitions require.

descriptor.title: Example Value
descriptor.doc: Example value from JSON Schema's "example" property. This is a valid value that passes all validation constraints.

descriptor.title: Constraint
descriptor.doc: Validation constraint enforced at runtime (minLength, maxLength, minimum, maximum, pattern, etc.). Values not meeting these constraints are rejected with a validation error.

descriptor.title: Format
descriptor.doc: Semantic format annotation (email, date-time, uri, date, etc.). The format is validated - for example, "format: email" ensures valid email address syntax. Consider linking to schema.org definitions for common formats.

descriptor.title: Enum
descriptor.doc: Allowed values list. Only these exact values are accepted. Any other value is rejected with a validation error.

descriptor.title: Documentation Link
descriptor.doc: Links configured in apidoc.xml. Common links: openapi (OpenAPI spec for tooling), schemas (JSON Schema index for validation/form generation).
